children: Palm oil rises in Asian trading, driven by a technical rebound after four consecutive sessions of declines, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. India's decision to halve import duties on crude palm oil and soybean oil to 5% is also supporting prices, it says. Still, near-term sentiment is cautious following the recent price weakness, making sustained buying interest important, it adds. AmInvestment Bank advises traders to watch the CPO support level at around 4,700 ringgit a ton and resistance near 4,850 ringgit-4,900 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for December delivery is 34 ringgit higher at 4,803 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
